aj-fernandez--new-world-oscuro.description: Launched in 2014 as the first New World blend, this box-pressed Nicaraguan puro pairs a dark oscuro wrapper from Estelí with a Jalapa binder and filler from Estelí, Condega and Ometepe. It smokes with sweet cocoa, earth and roasted coffee over a steady pepper line, suited to an evening after a full meal.

thirds.notes: Sweet chocolate and earth open, with black pepper and a little orange on the retrohale.
Citrus and wood come forward with black and white pepper while the chocolate recedes.
Pepper grows stronger, and wood, leather and earth carry a long, smooth finish.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – New World Robusto review
Gotham Cigars – New World, review of four blends

aj-fernandez--new-world-connecticut.description: Released in 2015 as the lighter side of the New World family, it wraps Nicaraguan and Brazilian filler in a San Andrés binder and a US-grown Connecticut shade leaf. Cedar, cream and nuts lead, with a citrus edge and a touch of coffee; fuller than many shade cigars, it suits a morning or late-afternoon break.

thirds.notes: Sweet cedar and a creamy texture lead, with nuts on the finish and a floral hint through the nose.
A peanut-like note takes over, backed by a milky sweetness and light earth.
The flavours thin out to faint cocoa, spice and fading oak.

sources.title: halfwheel – New World Connecticut Toro review
Gotham Cigars – New World, review of four blends

aj-fernandez--new-world-cameroon.description: Released in 2018, this box-pressed cigar was AJ Fernandez's first to use a Cameroon wrapper, laid over a Nicaraguan binder and filler that includes leaf from his Estelí farms. It is gentler than its New World siblings: toast, almonds and cream with hay and oak, building slowly toward dark chocolate. A good choice for an unhurried afternoon.

thirds.notes: Toast and creamy almonds open, with hay, leather and white pepper on the retrohale.
Almonds stay in front as dark chocolate gains ground, with coffee and oak drifting in and out.
Dark chocolate takes the lead over almonds and earth, with a faint floral touch.

sources.title: halfwheel – New World Cameroon Churchill review
Gotham Cigars – New World, review of four blends

aj-fernandez--new-world-puro-especial.description: Blended by AJ Fernandez with his father Ismael and introduced in 2017, this Nicaraguan puro draws on several family farms, with a Criollo '98 wrapper from Finca San José and tobacco aged three to five years. It is peppery and mineral, with leather, cedar, coffee and a little cocoa, and is best kept for after dinner.

thirds.notes: Sharp pepper and a mineral note open, with an occasional flash of lime zest.
The mineral side returns, sometimes sharper, while the pepper eases a little.
Coffee and a creamy edge appear among the minerals, with more pepper toward the end.

sources.title: halfwheel – New World Puro Especial Short Churchill review
Gotham Cigars – New World, review of four blends

aj-fernandez--new-world-dorado.description: Introduced in 2022, the Dorado is a Nicaraguan puro with a sun-grown wrapper and a binder and filler taken from a single farm in Estelí. It stays medium for most of the smoke, moving from dry cedar and cocoa to vanilla, caramel and leather, with coffee along the way. Easy company for an afternoon espresso.

thirds.notes: Dry cedar opens, then cocoa and black pepper over a creamy texture.
A vanilla sweetness joins the cocoa and leather as espresso moves forward.
Cocoa leads over leather and baking spice, and the body fills out slightly.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – New World Dorado Toro review

aj-fernandez--new-world-decenio.description: Made at the San Lotano factory in Ocotal and released in 2025 to mark ten years of New World, the Decenio pairs a Mexican San Andrés wrapper and Nicaraguan binder with Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. It opens with pepper, espresso and dry cocoa, then grows more refined, with cedar and vanilla carrying the later stages.

thirds.notes: Black pepper, toast, espresso and dry cocoa, with a vanilla note carried over from the cold draw.
The flavours knit together: espresso and cocoa, cleaner earth and cedar, with passing nutty and floral touches.
Rather than gaining power, the smoke narrows to a cleaner, cedar-led finish.

sources.title: Cigar Aficionado – New A.J. Fernandez cigar honors 10 years of New World
Cigar Reviews by the Katman – New World Decenio

aj-fernandez--san-lotano-requiem-habano.description: First released in 2010 as San Lotano Habano and made at AJ Fernandez's factory in Estelí, this blend sets a Brazilian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. It is spicy and woody, with dark chocolate, burnt caramel and leather, later joined by nuts and roasted coffee; a cigar for those who like pepper with their sweetness.

thirds.notes: Cedar, dark chocolate and burnt caramel meet pepper and spice, with leather on the finish.
A nutty note arrives as earth, leather and wood deepen, with pepper building on the retrohale.
Roasted coffee joins in and pepper takes the front, with the caramel returning on the finish.

sources.title: halfwheel – San Lotano Habano review
Cigar Inspector – San Lotano Requiem Habano Gran Toro

aj-fernandez--san-lotano-requiem-maduro.description: The maduro member of the San Lotano Requiem family wraps Nicaraguan and Honduran filler in a Honduran binder and a dark, oily San Andrés leaf from Mexico. It begins with pepper before cocoa, coffee and caramel settle in with a creamy texture, and the strength builds toward the end. Suited to a slow evening.

thirds.notes: A peppery start gives way to cocoa, coffee and caramel, soon smoothed by cream.
The spice recedes as cocoa and cream lead, before cedar and cinnamon surge back.
Intensity peaks, spice returns and the strength climbs to full without harshness.

sources.title: Cigar Reviews by the Katman – San Lotano Maduro
Cigar Press – AJ Fernandez San Lotano Maduro

aj-fernandez--san-lotano-requiem-connect.description: Released in 2010 within the San Lotano family, this blend combines an Ecuador-grown Connecticut shade wrapper with a Honduran binder and filler from Nicaragua, Honduras and the Dominican Republic. It carries more flavour than most shade cigars: white pepper, cedar and vanilla over a sweet, creamy base, with nuts toward the end. A fit for the morning.

thirds.notes: Sweetness, black pepper and a light fruit note, with nuts appearing midway.
Cedar and cream build and vanilla becomes clear, with gentle spice underneath.
The flavours ease to cream, nuts, cedar and a little earth, with spice returning near the end.

sources.title: Cigar Reviews by the Katman – San Lotano Connecticut
Cigar Coop – San Lotano Connecticut

aj-fernandez--san-lotano-the-bull.description: Introduced around 2013, The Bull is a box-pressed San Lotano blend with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and filler. It opens with spice, leather and cedar, then adds cocoa, cinnamon and light coffee, gaining body and a creamy texture as it burns. One for experienced smokers with time to spare.

sources.title: Cigar Reviews by the Katman – San Lotano The Bull
Cigar Czars – San Lotano The Bull review

thirds.notes: Pepper and spice that fade, with leather, cedar and cocoa, and light coffee and cinnamon behind.
Creamier and more balanced, with leather and cedar and a return of mild pepper.
Little change in flavour, though the cedar becomes more noticeable.

aj-fernandez--san-lotano-oval.description: Introduced in 2011, the San Lotano Oval is pressed into an oval cross-section, a shape new to the industry at the time. An Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper covers a Nicaraguan binder and filler of Nicaraguan and Honduran leaf. Citrus, cedar and spice open, followed by cocoa, espresso and nuts with a creamy finish.

thirds.notes: Bright citrus and cedary spice tingle on the retrohale, with cream and roasted nuts close behind.
The spice softens as dark cocoa and espresso come forward, with hints of dried cherry and earth.
A creamy texture leads with coffee, cocoa, nuts and mild cedar; the tingle returns without harshness.

sources.title: Half Ashed – San Lotano Oval Robusto review
Cigar Reviews by the Katman – San Lotano Oval

aj-fernandez--san-lotano-oval-maduro.description: The maduro version of the oval-pressed San Lotano, introduced in 2012, wraps a Nicaraguan binder and a filler that includes Honduran and Nicaraguan leaf in a dark maduro wrapper. Pepper and spice lead early, then cocoa, espresso, leather and earth settle in, and the strength builds steadily through the second half.

thirds.notes: Strong pepper settles over cocoa, leather, cedar and deep earth, with cream arriving after an inch.
The spice fades as espresso, cocoa and cream grow, with a touch of dried fruit.
Cocoa stays in front, a little spice returns and the strength keeps rising.

sources.title: halfwheel – San Lotano Oval Maduro Corona review
Cigar Reviews by the Katman – San Lotano Oval Maduro

aj-fernandez--san-lotano-oval-connecticu.description: Shown at the 2013 IPCPR trade show, this oval-pressed San Lotano pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper with a Nicaraguan binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. It is livelier than its pale wrapper suggests: white and black pepper first, then cream, roasted nuts and a charred wood note that firms up toward the end.

thirds.notes: Pepper on the palate and through the nose, smoothing after an inch into cream and a chalky note.
Roasted nuts appear and a charred wood note replaces the creaminess.
The char grows, the strength builds and pepper sharpens on the tip of the tongue.

sources.title: halfwheel – San Lotano Oval Connecticut Petit Robusto review

aj-fernandez--enclave.description: Released in 2015, the Enclave covers Nicaraguan filler, including Piloto Cubano, with a Cameroon binder and an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper. The smoke is buttery and toasty, with graham-cracker sweetness, cedar and black pepper, and finishes on walnut and pecan. A rounded choice for an afternoon with coffee.

thirds.notes: Buttery sweet tobacco and toast, with faint chocolate and black pepper in a creamy smoke.
Toast and butter persist; cedar shows on the retrohale before giving way to pepper and light spice.
Walnut and pecan join the toast as the smoke grows richer, with traces of butter and cedar.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – AJ Fernandez Enclave review
Gotham Cigars – Enclave Natural & Broadleaf review

aj-fernandez--enclave-broadleaf.description: Added to the Enclave line in 2017, this version uses a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and filler from Estelí, Jalapa and Pueblo Nuevo. It sits in a darker register: chocolate, earth, coffee and leather with a tart dried-fruit note and slow-building pepper. Strength runs between medium-full and full, so it belongs after a meal.

thirds.notes: Sweet-tart dried apricot opens, then a slow pepper warmth and chocolate over a creamy texture.
Fruit, chocolate and earth shift toward light-roast coffee as the strength edges up.
The tang sharpens toward sourness and a brief white pepper note passes.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – Enclave Broadleaf Robusto review
Gotham Cigars – Enclave Natural & Broadleaf review

aj-fernandez--bellas-artes.description: Introduced in 2016, Bellas Artes uses AJ Fernandez's own hybrid wrapper, a cross of Connecticut Shade, Corojo '99 and Havana 2000, over a Quilalí binder and filler from Nicaragua, Honduras and Brazil, each leaf aged at least three years. It starts peppery, then turns to wood, honey, dark chocolate and espresso, closing with citrus and cream.

thirds.notes: Cayenne and black pepper over dry wood, with vanilla, honey and nuts underneath.
Sweeter pepper and baking spice, now with dark chocolate, cedar, espresso and leather.
Pepper and spice return with an orange tang and cream, as the chocolate fades.

sources.title: Gotham Cigars – Bellas Artes Nicaraguan Hybrid

aj-fernandez--bellas-artes-maduro.description: The maduro edition of Bellas Artes arrived in 2018 with a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper, a Mexican San Andrés binder and filler from Estelí. It opens with a strong pepper bite before chocolate, coffee, cream and nuts come through, then turns savoury and earthy with a hint of licorice. Strength reaches full by the end.

thirds.notes: Intense black pepper with sweetened coffee, cream and dark chocolate.
The pepper eases and chocolate, coffee, nuts and cream fill in, with traces of leather.
Peppery, savoury and earthy, with chocolate and cream underneath as the strength reaches full.

sources.title: Cigar Reviews by the Katman – Bellas Artes Maduro
Klaro Cigars – Bellas Artes Maduro review

aj-fernandez--the-last-call.description: AJ Fernandez first rolled this blend for himself as the final cigar of his evenings, before releasing it in 2016 in a set of short formats. An Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler from his Estelí farms. Cedar, oak and vanilla meet a strong pepper retrohale, with leather and citrus later on.

thirds.notes: Black pepper up front with cedar, coffee, leather and a citrus tang.
The pepper settles; cedar and citrus lead, with vanilla sweetness and oak.
Citrus and oak stay, leather grows and the pepper turns to baking spice, closing on nuts and earth.

sources.title: Gotham Cigars – Last Call, from private stash to full production
The Cigar Authority – Last Call Habano Geniales review

aj-fernandez--the-last-call-maduro.description: The maduro counterpart of The Last Call swaps the Ecuadorian wrapper for dark Pennsylvania Broadleaf over Nicaraguan binder and filler from AJ Fernandez's Estelí farms. Pepper, leather and charred wood lead before a molasses-like sweetness, orange rind and cashew take over. A compact, dense smoke for the end of the evening.

thirds.notes: Black pepper, a mineral note, leather and charred wood.
A molasses-like sweetness builds with leather, orange rind and the first hint of cashew.
Cashew leads with charred wood, while leather and pepper linger on the finish.

sources.title: Gotham Cigars – Last Call, from private stash to full production
The Cigar Authority – Last Call Maduro Pequenas review

aj-fernandez--dias-de-gloria.description: Released in 2019, Días de Gloria is a sun-grown Nicaraguan puro made from Estelí tobacco aged for up to seven years, a nod to Cuban cigars of the pre-revolution era. Cedar, leather and toasted spice set the tone, with hay and cream along the way, and the strength builds steadily without turning harsh.

thirds.notes: Red pepper and toasted spice open, settling into cedar, leather, hay and a creamy smoke.
Leather, almond and cream, with drier spices such as cinnamon and nutmeg building.
Cedar and cream carry the close, with spice in waves and no harshness.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Días de Gloria Short Churchill review
Klaro Cigars – Días de Gloria review

aj-fernandez--dias-de-gloria-brazil.description: Introduced in 2024, this edition of Días de Gloria trades the Nicaraguan wrapper for a Brazilian Mata Fina leaf over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Cedar, Brazil nut and cocoa open with a touch of cinnamon, before bittersweet chocolate, moist earth and coffee grounds take over. Medium in strength, with a darker character than the original.

thirds.notes: Cedar with Brazil nut, a milky note, and cocoa touched by cinnamon and chili.
The cedar turns resinous as damp earth, dark chocolate and rum-soaked raisin come forward.
Bittersweet cocoa leads over earthy soil and coffee grounds.

sources.title: Klaro Cigars – Días de Gloria Brazil review

aj-fernandez--amar.description: Made at the San Lotano factory in Ocotal, Amar is a Nicaraguan puro under a Habano wrapper, created as thanks for the support AJ Fernandez received after a fire at his Estelí factory; the name nods to both Spanish and his Lebanese roots. Citrus, wood and roasted nuts lead a smooth, medium smoke with coffee at its centre.

thirds.notes: Bright citrus and a mineral edge with dry earth, wood, toast and a little coffee.
Roasted peanut and walnut, light coffee, vanilla cream and lemon, with a sweet floral touch.
Roasted nuts and fresh bread around coffee, as the spice spreads and the strength rises.

sources.title: Cigar Reviews by the Katman – AJ Fernandez Amar

aj-fernandez--havoc.description: Havoc is an all-Nicaraguan blend from AJ Fernandez, with wrapper, binder and filler grown in Nicaragua. Leather and cedar lead over dry earth and baking spice, the finish stays creamy throughout, and pepper takes over in the last third with a hint of mocha. Medium-full in strength, it suits a long evening.

thirds.notes: Smooth leather with cedar, dry earth and baking spice, light pepper on the retrohale and a creamy finish.
Sweet and baking spices move forward with white pepper, leather and cedar.
Black and white pepper lead, leather and earth stay, and the retrohale adds mocha.

sources.title: JR Cigar Blending Room – Havoc by A.J. Fernandez

aj-fernandez--nicaraguan-series.description: An everyday Nicaraguan puro from AJ Fernandez's Estelí factory, the Nicaraguan Series uses wrapper, binder and filler grown in Nicaragua. It opens with red pepper, cinnamon and cream over chocolate and caramel, turns to black pepper with more layers, and finishes with raisin and almond as the strength grows.

thirds.notes: Bold red pepper, cinnamon, cream and chocolate, with a caramel sweetness.
Black pepper replaces the red, and the flavours become more layered with a long finish.
Black pepper, chocolate, raisin, almond and toffee, with no harshness.

sources.title: JR Cigar Blending Room – Nicaraguan Series by AJ Fernandez
Cigar Reviews by the Katman – Nicaraguan Series Robusto

aj-fernandez--blend-15.description: Blend 15 is a long-filler Nicaraguan puro sold in paper bundles of fifteen, the first bundle cigar to carry the AJ Fernandez name. It was made for markets outside the United States, with Germany among the first, and comes in short robusto, robusto and toro sizes.

sources.title: halfwheel – Blend 15 by AJ Fernandez scheduled for November
Cigars Lover – AJ Fernandez Blend 15 Robusto

thirds.notes: Earth and leather over a lightly spicy base led by black pepper.
The spices grow slightly, and the vegetal notes of the opening come back.
The same profile carries on with a balanced finish as the strength rises.

aj-fernandez--20th-anniversary.description: Shown at the 2024 PCA trade show to mark AJ Fernandez's twentieth anniversary, this limited Nicaraguan puro was made from tobacco selected from his best stock. The 6 x 56 toro came in 7,500 lacquered boxes of 20, alongside 250 commemorative humidors holding a belicoso.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – AJ Fernandez 20th Anniversary debuts at 2024 PCA
